caveats: ⚑ Hit Rate ▲5.44% (all allies) and ▲3.79% (SMG allies) map to hitRatePct, whose core-hit lift (sim.ts hrCoreMult) is a DERIVED magnitude, not a kit quantity — the damage consequence of both lines is unmeasured for this unit.

⚑ Cadence/reload tuple is datamine-sourced (SMG; ammo 120, reloadFrames 107) and per modeling-priors is the #1 uniform-heat cause. SMG is also the one class where nominal rate does not divide 60fps evenly, so the effective rate differs from nominal — verify against an ammo-counter read before trusting any hitCount:30 proc frequency.

⚑ hitCount:30 is keyed to LANDED normal attacks ('after landing 30'). The engine's hitCount fires on the owner's hits; if SMG landing fraction < 1 in-game, the real proc interval is longer than the sim's. Unmeasured.

skill2 block 3 'for 1 round(s)' is encoded as durationShots:1 per the ROUND-count rule (expires after the HOLDER fires 1 round, spanning reloads) — NOT wall-clock. On a fast-firing holder this window is ~1 frame-interval and contributes almost nothing; a wall-clock misread would massively over-credit. Flagged for judge scrutiny, but the text is literal.

'except the skill user; including the skill user if there are not enough allies' is encoded as excludeSelf:true. The fallback self-inclusion branch is not expressible in TargetDef and is moot on a full 5-unit team (there are always enough allies).
'highest final ATK' is literal → byFinalAtk:true (live effectiveAtk ranking) on both the skill2 single-target block and the burst 2-target block, per the A3 literal-word rule.

Every skill1/skill2 line is a stat buff with no damage rider, DoT, weapon-swap, heal/shield, gauge, ammo, or reload component — there is nothing in this kit for the FB-timing (noFb) or range rules to apply to, and no ⚑ is owed for them.

Burst is keyed to burstCast (this unit's own Burst I cast), not fullBurstEnter — a Burst I buff block fires on the rotations THIS unit casts. skill2's three blocks say 'entering Full Burst' literally, so they are fullBurstEnter (any team Full Burst), not burstCast.
override.note: PARSER BASELINE (HYPOTHESIS — NOT a validated model). Every ⚑ below is an UNMEASURED estimate; hand-tune + record against a real fight before trusting any number. Blind second read of the kit prose only (BLIND-STUDY, VALUES-WITHHELD): no override, tests, DECISIONS, probe data, or board output consulted. Pure support kit — 7 kit lines, all stat buffs, zero damage riders, zero weapon-state modifiers, zero heal/shield/gauge lines, so `unmodeled` is empty for all three slots (no silent drops). The three load-bearing judgment calls: (1) skill1's three lines share ONE trigger ('after landing 30 normal attacks') but THREE distinct target sets (all allies / SMG allies / self), so they are three blocks, and the SMG-scoped Hit Rate stacks additively on top of the all-ally Hit Rate for SMG holders including this unit; (2) skill2's 'for 1 round(s)' crit-rate grant is a ROUND count (durationShots:1), never 1 second — a seconds misread would be a large over-credit; (3) skill2 uses fullBurstEnter (text: 'when entering Full Burst' — fires on ANY team Full Burst) while the burst slot uses burstCast, which is the burstCast-vs-fullBurstEnter fidelity split. Damage-relevant risk is concentrated in the two hitRatePct lines (derived core-lift magnitude) and in the SMG cadence that sets the hitCount:30 proc rate.

flags.estimate: Ship the kit-literal percentages 5.44 and 3.79 into hitRatePct; the resulting core-hit lift is whatever sim.ts hrCoreMult yields (HRCORE=1 default).
flags.reasoning: ALWAYS-⚑ #7: the Hit-Rate→core magnitude is measured-only. The kit gives a Hit Rate percentage, but the mapping from that percentage to actual core-hit frequency (and therefore damage) is an engine-derived relationship, not a kit quantity. Both lines are team-wide, so any error here scales across the whole comp, and the two stack additively on SMG holders (9.23% combined for this unit and any SMG ally) — the largest single damage lever in an otherwise pure stat-buff kit.
flags.recipe: Record a comp with and without this unit at fixed gear and count CORE HIT (red) popups per 100 landed rounds on an SMG ally during the 5s window vs outside it; the delta in core rate per point of Hit Rate calibrates hrCoreMult. Cross-check with the accuracy-circle geometry in docs/data/sg-calc/ (owner ruling: the geometry is ground truth and outranks damage-back-derived core rates).

flags.field: cadence tuple — pullsPerSec / reloadFrames (base stats: ammo 120, reloadFrames 107)
flags.estimate: Engine default SMG cadence + datamined reloadFrames 107. Note SMG's nominal 1440 rpm = 2.5 frames does not divide 60fps evenly, so the effective rate is 60/ceil(2.5)=20.0/s, not 24/s.
flags.reasoning: ALWAYS-⚑ #1: rate_of_fire and reloadFrames are known-unreliable datamine fields, and prior 1 names cadence as the #1 cause of uniform heat. For THIS unit the cadence is doubly load-bearing because it sets how often the hitCount:30 trigger fires — the entire skill1 buff uptime (three simultaneous buffs, two of them team-wide) is a direct function of shots/sec. A 20% cadence error becomes a ~20% error in skill1 proc frequency, which propagates to every ally.
flags.recipe: Two-frame ammo-counter read 0.5s apart in a no-reload window, repeated in a second range band (docs/modeling-priors.md 'Measuring fire cadence'). The ammo counter measures shots/sec directly; do NOT use FB counts, which measure gauge/sec and cannot discriminate the two. Separately time a full reload from empty to confirm 107f.

flags.field: skill1[*].trigger — hitCount:30 semantics (landed hits vs rounds fired)
flags.estimate: hitCount:30 as written; assume ~100% landing so the proc interval ≈ 30 rounds ≈ 1.5s at 20/s.
flags.reasoning: The text says 'after LANDING 30 normal attack(s)', not 'after firing'. The engine's hitCount trigger counts the owner's hits. If real SMG landing fraction is below 1 (accuracy circle at range), the true interval is longer than the sim's and skill1 uptime is over-credited. With a 5s duration on a ~1.5s nominal interval the buffs are effectively permanent, which makes the model INSENSITIVE to moderate cadence error in one direction — but a large landing shortfall could break that saturation. Cannot be resolved from text.
flags.recipe: From a recording, count this unit's landed hits (popup count) over a 10s window and compare to rounds spent off the ammo counter; the ratio is the landing fraction. Then verify the buff actually saturates: tap buffApply events for stat hitRatePct/atkPct and confirm re-application interval < 5s over the whole fight (not just the opening).

flags.estimate: durationShots:1 — expires right after the recipient's next single round.
flags.reasoning: Not a value I invented, but a semantics call worth surfacing: 'for 1 round(s)' is the ROUND-count primitive, so an 85.42% crit-rate grant lasts exactly ONE bullet on the highest-final-ATK ally. That is a very large number attached to a near-zero window, which is the shape most likely to be misread as 1 second (a ~10-60x over-credit depending on the holder's fire rate). The engine decrements after the shot's blocks dispatch, so the recipient's first post-FB-entry round does benefit. Whether the in-game window is genuinely one bullet or has an implicit floor is not verifiable from text.
flags.recipe: Put a slow-firing high-ATK ally (SR/RL) in the comp, enter Full Burst, and check whether exactly one of that ally's shots crits at the elevated rate vs a sustained run of crits. Read the buffApply event's durationShots field and count damage events between apply and drop.
